In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat an-Nas

It is Meccan (Madaniyya in the text).

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾. He is the Shaytan (Satan), and the meaning is: from the evil of the Shaytan, the one with the whisperings. It is said: he was named "whisperer" (waswas) because he squats (yajthum), so when the servant remembers his Lord he withdraws (khanasa), i.e. draws back, and when he does not remember, he whispers.

In another narration: he seizes (iltaqama) and whispers, i.e. the heart.

And there is a sound hadith with this meaning.

As for His words: ﴿al-Khannas﴾, its meaning is what we have said, namely: when the servant remembers his Lord and glorifies Him, he retreats, i.e. draws back, withdraws and keeps away.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"And His saying: ﴿Who whispers into the breasts of mankind﴾ is Satan."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 114, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿from the jinn﴾, meaning: from the jinn.

And His saying: ﴿and mankind﴾, meaning: and from mankind.

The meaning is that He commanded him to seek refuge from the devils of the jinn and of mankind. The shaytan (devil) is every rebellious one, whether he is a jinn or a human. It is reported in the well-known traditions that "when the Prophet wished to sleep, he would recite Surat al-Ikhlas and the two Mu'awwidhatayn (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and blow into his palms, then wipe with his palms as much of his body as he could, beginning with his face and head."

It is also related that he used to seek refuge with them for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi mentioned, through the narration of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated to me, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, from the Prophet, that he said: "Allah the Exalted has sent down upon me verses the like of which have never been seen: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ to the end of the surah, and ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾ to the end of the surah." He said: "This is a hadith that is hasan sahih."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Abd Allah 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu al-'Abbas ibn Siraj al-Sabakhi informed us, Abu al-'Abbas ibn Mahbub informed us, Abu 'Isa al-Hafiz informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid... the hadith.

If someone asks: Why did Ibn Mas'ud not write these two surahs in his codex? Is it possible that someone might be confused as to whether they are from the Qur'an or not? The answer: Hammad ibn Salama narrated from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Ibn Mas'ud did not write the two Mu'awwidhatayn in his codex!" Ubayy said: "The Messenger of Allah said: 'Jibril, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾, so I recited it, and he said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾, so I recited it.'" So we say what the Messenger of Allah said.

It seems that Ubayy agreed with Ibn Mas'ud.

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Naqqur informed us of this hadith, Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababa informed us, al-Baghawi informed us, Hudba informed us, from Hammad ibn Salama.

The hadith is recorded by Muslim in the Sahih. It is possible that Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy, from the frequency with which they heard the Prophet recite these two surahs and seek refuge with them, thought they were a charm (ruqya/'awdha), so they did not affirm them in the Mushaf. It has also been said that they are written in the codex of Ubayy.

Some have mentioned that 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud was not confused about whether they were from the Qur'an, but did not write them down because of their fame, just as the writing of Surat al-Fatiha was omitted because of its fame. And Allah knows best and is most wise, and the correct view is with Him, and to Him is the return and the final place.

May Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad and his family, all of them, and grant abundant peace.
